title: An Interview with Nikola Tesla
subject: English
chapter: 8. Prose: An Interview with Nikola Tesla
description: Grammar-focused practice for the chapter: kinds of adjectives (quality, quantity, number, demonstrative, interrogative) and degrees of comparison (positive, comparative, superlative), with prose comprehension, vocabulary, and idioms from 'An Interview with Nikola Tesla'.

questions.question: What is an adjective?
options: A word that describes a noun or pronoun
A word that names a person or place
A word that joins two sentences
questions.explanation: An adjective is a describing word — it tells us more about a noun or pronoun.

questions.question: What do adjectives of quality describe?
options: The kind or nature of a noun
questions.explanation: Adjectives of quality describe the kind or nature of a noun and answer the question 'What kind?'.

questions.question: In 'The brave firefighter rescued the child', which word is an adjective of quality?
questions.explanation: 'brave' describes the kind of firefighter, so it is an adjective of quality.

questions.question: In 'The smart robot can solve complex puzzles', which words are adjectives of quality?
questions.explanation: 'smart' describes the robot and 'complex' describes the puzzles — both are adjectives of quality.

questions.question: Adjectives of quality answer the question 'What kind?'.
questions.explanation: Adjectives of quality describe the kind or nature of a noun, answering 'What kind?'.

questions.question: Which word is an adjective of quality in 'The ancient Colosseum attracts tourists'?
questions.explanation: 'ancient' describes what kind of Colosseum, so it is an adjective of quality.

questions.question: Select ALL the adjectives of quality.
questions.explanation: 'colourful' and 'majestic' describe the kind of noun (quality). 'three' is number and 'those' is demonstrative.

questions.question: Which sentence contains an adjective of quality?
options: The tall building has many windows.
questions.explanation: 'tall' describes the kind of building, so it is an adjective of quality. ('many' is quantity.)

questions.question: Which of these is an adjective of quality?
questions.explanation: 'beautiful' describes the kind or nature of a noun, so it is an adjective of quality.

questions.question: In 'Nikola Tesla was a brilliant inventor', which word is the adjective of quality?
questions.explanation: 'brilliant' describes what kind of inventor Tesla was, so it is an adjective of quality.

questions.question: Which word describes the noun in 'colourful coral reefs'?
questions.explanation: 'colourful' describes the kind of reefs, so it is the adjective of quality. ('coral' names the type of reef.)

questions.question: In 'the enormous Amazon Rainforest', the word 'enormous' is an adjective of quality.
questions.explanation: 'enormous' describes the kind/size of the rainforest, so it is an adjective of quality.

questions.question: Adjectives of quality help to ____.
options: paint a vivid picture in the reader's mind
point out which noun is meant
questions.explanation: Adjectives of quality are commonly used and help paint a vivid picture by describing the noun's characteristics.

questions.question: Which sentence uses TWO adjectives of quality?
options: The old, wise scientist made a discovery.
questions.explanation: 'old' and 'wise' both describe the kind of scientist, so both are adjectives of quality.

questions.question: Which word could describe the quality of a 'car'?
questions.explanation: 'sleek' describes the kind/appearance of the car, so it is an adjective of quality.

questions.question: Which is an adjective of quality in 'His groundbreaking work changed the world'?
questions.explanation: 'groundbreaking' describes the kind of work, so it is an adjective of quality.

questions.question: The word 'brave' in 'the brave firefighter' is an adjective of quality.
questions.explanation: 'brave' tells us what kind of firefighter, so it is an adjective of quality.

questions.question: Select ALL the adjectives of quality in 'The clever, curious student asked deep questions'.
questions.explanation: 'clever', 'curious', and 'deep' all describe the kind of noun, so all three are adjectives of quality. 'student' is a noun.

questions.question: Which word is NOT an adjective of quality?
questions.explanation: 'many' is an adjective of quantity (how much/how many). 'shiny', 'soft', and 'bright' describe the kind of noun.

questions.question: An adjective of quality gives information about the ____ of a noun.
questions.explanation: Adjectives of quality provide information about the specific characteristic or attribute of the noun they modify.

questions.question: What do adjectives of quantity tell us?
options: How much of something there is
What kind of thing it is
Which one is being pointed to
questions.explanation: Adjectives of quantity indicate how much of something is being referred to, answering 'How much?'.

questions.question: Adjectives of quantity are often used with which kind of noun?
questions.explanation: Adjectives of quantity are often used with uncountable nouns, telling us the amount or extent.

questions.question: In 'Many ancient manuscripts were damaged', which word is the adjective of quantity?
questions.explanation: 'Many' tells us how much/how many, so it is an adjective of quantity. ('ancient' is quality.)

questions.question: Adjectives of quantity answer the question 'How much?'.
questions.explanation: Adjectives of quantity tell us how much of something there is, answering 'How much?'.

questions.question: Which word is an adjective of quantity?
questions.explanation: 'some' tells us the amount of something, so it is an adjective of quantity.

questions.question: Select ALL the adjectives of quantity.
questions.explanation: 'much' and 'little' tell us the amount (quantity). 'tall' is quality and 'those' is demonstrative.

questions.question: In 'There is enough electricity to create a second sun', which word shows quantity?
questions.explanation: 'enough' tells us the amount of electricity, so it is an adjective of quantity.

questions.question: Which sentence uses an adjective of quantity correctly with an uncountable noun?
questions.explanation: 'little' (quantity) works with the uncountable noun 'water'. The others use countable nouns, which need words like 'few'.

questions.question: Which word tells us the amount in 'He has some money'?
questions.explanation: 'some' tells us the amount of money, so it is an adjective of quantity.

questions.question: The word 'countless' in 'countless ski trails' shows quantity.
questions.explanation: 'countless' tells us there are very many trails — an amount — so it is an adjective of quantity.

questions.question: Which word is an adjective of quantity in 'Hundreds of fish swim in the deep waters'?
questions.explanation: 'Hundreds of' shows the amount of fish, so it is an adjective of quantity. ('deep' is quality.)

questions.question: Which of these is an adjective of quantity?
questions.explanation: 'all' tells us the amount/extent, so it is an adjective of quantity.

questions.question: Adjectives of quantity help to specify the ____ of the noun they modify.
questions.explanation: Adjectives of quantity help specify the amount or extent of the noun they modify.

questions.question: Select ALL the words that can be adjectives of quantity.
questions.explanation: 'enough', 'some', and 'many' all show amount (quantity). 'beautiful' is an adjective of quality.

questions.question: Which sentence contains an adjective of quantity?
options: We need more time to finish.
questions.explanation: 'more' tells us the amount of time, so it is an adjective of quantity.

questions.question: What do adjectives of number tell us?
options: How many of something, or the order they appear in
What kind of thing it is
How much of something there is
questions.explanation: Adjectives of number indicate how many of something there are, or the order in which they appear.

questions.question: In 'The scientist discovered one rare species', which word is an adjective of number?
questions.explanation: 'one' tells us how many species, so it is an adjective of number (a definite numeral).

questions.question: In 'The third chapter explains Newton's laws', which word is an adjective of number?
questions.explanation: 'third' shows the position/order, so it is an adjective of number (an ordinal adjective).

questions.question: Words like 'one', 'two', and 'three' are called ____.
questions.explanation: 'One', 'two', and 'three' are definite numeral adjectives, indicating a specific quantity.

questions.question: Words like 'first', 'second', and 'third' are called ____.
questions.explanation: 'First', 'second', and 'third' are ordinal adjectives, showing a specific position in a sequence.

questions.question: Words like 'several', 'all', and 'no' are called ____.
questions.explanation: 'Several', 'all', and 'no' are indefinite numeral adjectives, indicating a general (not exact) quantity.

questions.question: Adjectives of number can answer the question 'How many?' or 'In what order?'.
questions.explanation: Adjectives of number tell us how many of something there are, or the order in which they appear.

questions.question: In 'The first satellite launched by India was Aryabhata', which is the adjective of number?
questions.explanation: 'first' shows the order/position, so it is an ordinal adjective of number.

questions.question: Select ALL the adjectives of number.
questions.explanation: 'four' (definite), 'ninth' (ordinal), and 'second' (ordinal) are adjectives of number. 'many' is quantity.

questions.question: In 'four marble minarets', which word is the adjective of number?
questions.explanation: 'four' tells us how many minarets, so it is an adjective of number.

questions.question: Which sentence uses an ordinal adjective?
options: She came second in the race.
questions.explanation: 'second' shows position/order in the race, so it is an ordinal adjective of number.

questions.question: 'No' in 'no students were absent' is an indefinite numeral adjective.
questions.explanation: 'no' indicates a general quantity (none), so it is an indefinite numeral adjective of number.

questions.question: Which word tells us how many in 'nine countries'?
questions.explanation: 'nine' tells us how many countries, so it is an adjective of number.

questions.question: Which sentence uses a definite numeral adjective?
options: The porridge needs two ripe bananas.
questions.explanation: 'two' is a definite numeral adjective — it gives an exact number. The others show general quantity.

questions.question: Select ALL the ordinal adjectives.
questions.explanation: 'first', 'fifth', and 'second' show position in a sequence, so they are ordinal adjectives. 'twenty' is a definite numeral.

questions.question: Which of these is an adjective of number?
questions.explanation: 'ten' tells us how many, so it is an adjective of number (a definite numeral).

questions.question: Which type of number adjective is 'several'?
questions.explanation: 'several' shows a general, not exact, quantity, so it is an indefinite numeral adjective.

questions.question: 'Third' is an ordinal adjective because it shows a position in a sequence.
questions.explanation: 'third' shows a specific position or order, so it is an ordinal adjective of number.

questions.question: In 'Tesla held over 300 patents', which word is the adjective of number?
questions.explanation: '300' tells us how many patents, so it is a definite numeral adjective of number.

questions.question: Which sentence has an indefinite numeral adjective?
questions.explanation: 'All' shows a general quantity, so it is an indefinite numeral adjective. The others are definite or ordinal.

questions.question: What do demonstrative adjectives do?
options: Point out which noun is being referred to
Ask a question about the noun
questions.explanation: Demonstrative adjectives point out which noun or pronoun is being referred to, answering 'Which?'.

questions.question: Which of these is a list of the demonstrative adjectives?
questions.explanation: The demonstrative adjectives are 'this', 'that', 'these', and 'those'.

questions.question: In 'This monument was built long ago', which word is the demonstrative adjective?
questions.explanation: 'This' points out which monument, so it is a demonstrative adjective.

questions.question: Which demonstrative adjectives are used for things that are NEAR?
questions.explanation: 'this' and 'these' refer to things that are near, while 'that' and 'those' refer to things farther away.

questions.question: Which demonstrative adjectives are used for things that are FAR away?
questions.explanation: 'that' and 'those' refer to things that are farther away, while 'this' and 'these' refer to near things.

questions.question: Which demonstrative adjectives are used with SINGULAR nouns?
questions.explanation: 'this' and 'that' are used with singular nouns, while 'these' and 'those' are used with plural nouns.

questions.question: Which demonstrative adjectives are used with PLURAL nouns?
questions.explanation: 'these' and 'those' are used with plural nouns, while 'this' and 'that' are used with singular nouns.

questions.question: Demonstrative adjectives answer the question 'Which?'.
questions.explanation: Demonstrative adjectives point out which noun is meant, answering the question 'Which?'.

questions.question: Choose the correct demonstrative adjective: '____ shoes were handmade in Rajasthan.' (plural, far)
questions.explanation: 'Those' is used for plural nouns that are far away, so 'Those shoes' is correct.

questions.question: Choose the correct demonstrative adjective: '____ documents must be submitted before the interview.' (plural, near)
questions.explanation: 'These' is used for plural nouns that are near, so 'These documents' is correct.

questions.question: Which sentence uses a demonstrative adjective correctly with a singular noun?
questions.explanation: 'This' is used with singular nouns, so 'This book' is correct. The others mismatch singular/plural.

questions.question: In 'Those snowy Swiss Alps hold countless ski trails', which word is the demonstrative adjective?
questions.explanation: 'Those' points out which Alps (plural, far), so it is the demonstrative adjective. 'snowy' is quality.

questions.question: Select ALL the demonstrative adjectives.
questions.explanation: 'this' and 'those' point out which noun, so they are demonstrative. 'brave' is quality and 'many' is quantity.

questions.question: Choose the correct demonstrative: '____ painting captures the quiet dignity of rural women.' (singular, far)
questions.explanation: 'That' is used for a singular noun that is farther away, so 'That painting' is correct.

questions.question: We should say 'these dog' because 'these' can be used with any noun.
questions.explanation: 'these' is used only with plural nouns, so 'these dogs' is correct. For one dog, we say 'this dog'.

questions.question: Which sentence points to something near and singular?
questions.explanation: 'This' is used for something near and singular, so 'This pen is mine' fits.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses 'those'?
questions.explanation: 'those' is used with plural, far nouns, so 'Those mountains' is correct.

questions.question: In 'these historic grounds', which word is the demonstrative adjective?
questions.explanation: 'these' points out which grounds (plural, near), so it is the demonstrative adjective. 'historic' is quality.

questions.question: 'This' and 'that' are used with singular nouns.
questions.explanation: 'this' (near) and 'that' (far) are both used with singular nouns.

questions.question: Which sentence has an error in the demonstrative adjective?
questions.explanation: 'This' is singular but 'books' is plural — a mismatch. It should be 'These books are new'.

questions.question: What are interrogative adjectives used for?
options: To describe the kind of noun
To point out which noun is meant
To tell how many there are
questions.explanation: Interrogative adjectives are used to ask questions about nouns.

questions.question: Which words are the main interrogative adjectives?
questions.explanation: The main interrogative adjectives are 'which' and 'what'. 'Whose' can also work as one.

questions.question: In 'Which planet is known as the Red Planet?', which word is the interrogative adjective?
questions.explanation: 'Which' asks a question about the noun 'planet', so it is an interrogative adjective.

questions.question: In 'What was the name of the first man on the moon?', which word is the interrogative adjective?
questions.explanation: 'What' asks a question about the noun 'name', so it is an interrogative adjective.

questions.question: 'Whose' can also work as an interrogative adjective.
questions.explanation: Besides 'which' and 'what', the word 'whose' can also function as an interrogative adjective.

questions.question: In 'Which towering skyscrapers reach over fifty floors?', which word is the interrogative adjective?
questions.explanation: 'Which' asks a question about the skyscrapers, so it is the interrogative adjective. 'towering' is quality.

questions.question: Which sentence uses an interrogative adjective?
questions.explanation: 'What' asks a question about the noun 'time', so it is an interrogative adjective.

questions.question: Select ALL the interrogative adjectives.
questions.explanation: 'which' and 'what' ask questions about nouns, so they are interrogative. 'these' is demonstrative and 'brave' is quality.

questions.question: In 'Which river flows through Varanasi?', what does 'Which' do?
options: It asks a question about the noun 'river'
It describes the kind of river
It points to a river nearby
questions.explanation: 'Which' asks a question about the noun 'river', making it an interrogative adjective.

questions.question: An interrogative adjective always comes right before the noun it asks about.
questions.explanation: Interrogative adjectives like 'which' and 'what' come before a noun to ask a question about it, as in 'which book' or 'what colour'.

questions.question: Which sentence uses 'whose' as an interrogative adjective?
options: Whose bag is on the table?
The bag is on the table.
questions.explanation: 'Whose' asks a question about the noun 'bag' (who owns it), so it is used as an interrogative adjective.

questions.question: Which word begins a question about a noun in 'What colour is your shirt?'
questions.explanation: 'What' asks a question about the noun 'colour', so it is the interrogative adjective.

questions.question: Interrogative adjectives are used to ____.
questions.explanation: Interrogative adjectives ask questions about nouns, such as 'which', 'what', and 'whose'.

questions.question: Select ALL the sentences that use an interrogative adjective.
questions.explanation: 'Which shirt' and 'What game' ask questions about nouns (interrogative). The other two use demonstratives.

questions.question: Which of these is an interrogative adjective?
questions.explanation: 'which' asks a question about a noun, so it is an interrogative adjective.

questions.question: In 'This majestic Taj Mahal has four marble minarets', which word is a demonstrative adjective?
questions.explanation: 'This' points out which Taj Mahal, so it is demonstrative. 'majestic' and 'marble' are quality, and 'four' is number.

questions.question: In 'This majestic Taj Mahal has four marble minarets', which word is an adjective of number?
questions.explanation: 'four' tells us how many minarets, so it is an adjective of number.

questions.question: What kind of adjective is 'many' in 'many ancient manuscripts'?
questions.explanation: 'many' tells us the amount, so it is an adjective of quantity. ('ancient' is quality.)

questions.question: What kind of adjective is 'ancient' in 'the ancient Colosseum'?
questions.explanation: 'ancient' describes the kind of Colosseum, so it is an adjective of quality.

questions.question: In 'Which two brave soldiers guarded those gates?', match the adjectives. Select ALL that are correctly identified.
questions.explanation: 'Which' is interrogative, 'two' is number, and 'brave' is quality. 'those' is demonstrative, not quantity.

questions.question: What kind of adjective is 'those' in 'those historic grounds'?
questions.explanation: 'those' points out which grounds (plural, far), so it is a demonstrative adjective.

questions.question: In 'What amazing discovery did that brilliant scientist make?', which is the interrogative adjective?
questions.explanation: 'What' asks a question about 'discovery', so it is interrogative. 'that' is demonstrative; 'amazing' and 'brilliant' are quality.

questions.question: How many KINDS of adjectives are taught in this chapter?
questions.explanation: The chapter teaches five kinds: adjectives of quality, quantity, number, demonstrative adjectives, and interrogative adjectives.

questions.question: In 'The enormous Amazon Rainforest shelters many rare species', which word is an adjective of quantity?
questions.explanation: 'many' tells us the amount of species (quantity). 'enormous' and 'rare' are quality adjectives.

questions.question: In 'These five clever students answered which question?', select the CORRECT identifications.
questions.explanation: 'These' is demonstrative, 'five' is number, 'clever' is quality. 'which' is interrogative, not quantity.

questions.question: How many degrees of comparison are there?
questions.explanation: There are three degrees of comparison: positive, comparative, and superlative.

questions.question: What does the positive degree of an adjective do?
options: Describes a noun without comparing it
Asks a question about a noun
questions.explanation: The positive degree is the simplest form; it describes a noun without comparing it to anything.

questions.question: Which sentence uses an adjective in the positive degree?
options: The cat is faster than the dog.
The cat is the fastest of all.
questions.explanation: 'fast' with no comparison is the positive degree. 'faster' is comparative and 'fastest' is superlative.

questions.question: The positive degree simply describes a quality without comparing.
questions.explanation: The positive degree is the basic form of an adjective that describes a noun without comparison.

questions.question: Which is the positive form of the adjective in 'Jupiter is larger than Mars'?
questions.explanation: The positive (basic) form of 'larger' is 'large'.

questions.question: What does the comparative degree do?
questions.explanation: The comparative degree compares two nouns.

questions.question: How do we usually form the comparative of a short (one-syllable) adjective?
questions.explanation: For one-syllable adjectives, we usually add '-er', like 'tall → taller'.

questions.question: What is the comparative form of 'tall'?
questions.explanation: The comparative of 'tall' is 'taller' (add '-er').

questions.question: What is the comparative form of 'big'?
questions.explanation: 'big' ends in consonant-vowel-consonant (CVC), so we double the last consonant and add '-er': 'bigger'.

questions.question: What is the comparative form of 'nice'?
questions.explanation: 'nice' ends in 'e', so we just add 'r' to form the comparative: 'nicer'.

questions.question: How do we form the comparative of a long adjective like 'beautiful'?
questions.explanation: For adjectives with two or more syllables, we use 'more' before the adjective: 'more beautiful'.

questions.question: Which word usually follows a comparative adjective when comparing two things?
questions.explanation: When comparing two nouns, we use 'than' after the comparative, as in 'taller than'.

questions.question: Choose the correct comparative: 'The cheetah is ____ than most predators.'
questions.explanation: We are comparing two things with 'than', so we use the comparative 'faster'.

questions.question: The comparative degree is used to compare exactly two nouns.
questions.explanation: The comparative degree compares two nouns, often using 'than'.

questions.question: Choose the correct comparative: 'Leonardo da Vinci was ____ than many painters of his time.'
questions.explanation: 'famous' has more than one syllable, so we use 'more famous' for the comparative.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the comparative degree correctly?
options: Tesla's idea was more advanced than Edison's.
Tesla's idea was most advanced than Edison's.
Tesla's idea was advanced than Edison's.
questions.explanation: 'more advanced than' is the correct comparative form for the multi-syllable adjective 'advanced'.

questions.question: What is the comparative form of 'hot'?
questions.explanation: 'hot' follows the CVC pattern, so we double the 't' and add '-er': 'hotter'.

questions.question: Which is the CORRECT comparative sentence?
options: This box is heavier than that one.
This box is more heavier than that one.
This box is heaviest than that one.
This box is heavy than that one.
questions.explanation: 'heavier than' is the correct comparative. We never use 'more' with an '-er' form.

questions.question: Select ALL the correctly formed comparatives.
questions.explanation: 'wiser' (add r), 'bigger' (double + er), and 'more interesting' (use more) are correct. 'beautifuller' is wrong — it should be 'more beautiful'.

questions.question: What is the comparative form of 'wise'?
questions.explanation: 'wise' ends in 'e', so we add 'r': 'wiser'.

questions.question: What does the superlative degree do?
options: Asks a question about a noun
questions.explanation: The superlative degree compares three or more nouns, showing the highest degree of a quality.

questions.question: How do we usually form the superlative of a short (one-syllable) adjective?
questions.explanation: For one-syllable adjectives, we usually add '-est', like 'tall → tallest'.

questions.question: What is the superlative form of 'tall'?
questions.explanation: The superlative of 'tall' is 'tallest' (add '-est').

questions.question: What is the superlative form of 'big'?
questions.explanation: 'big' follows the CVC pattern, so we double the last consonant and add '-est': 'biggest'.

questions.question: What is the superlative form of 'large'?
questions.explanation: 'large' ends in 'e', so we add '-st': 'largest'.

questions.question: How do we form the superlative of a long adjective like 'beautiful'?
questions.explanation: For adjectives with two or more syllables, we use 'most' before the adjective: 'most beautiful'.

questions.question: Which word usually comes before a superlative adjective?
questions.explanation: We use 'the' before the superlative degree, as in 'the tallest' or 'the most famous'.

questions.question: Choose the correct superlative: 'Jupiter is the ____ planet in our solar system.'
questions.explanation: Comparing Jupiter with all the planets (three or more) needs the superlative 'largest'.

questions.question: We use 'the most' in the superlative degree to show the highest degree of something.
questions.explanation: The book reminds us that we use 'the most' in the superlative degree to show the highest degree of a quality.

questions.question: Choose the correct superlative: 'Leonardo da Vinci is one of the ____ painters in history.'
questions.explanation: 'famous' has more than one syllable, so the superlative is 'most famous'.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the superlative correctly?
options: Tesla is one of the greatest visionaries in science.
Tesla is one of the greater visionaries in science.
Tesla is one of the most greatest visionaries.
Tesla is one of the great visionaries than others.
questions.explanation: 'the greatest' is the correct superlative form for comparing Tesla with all other visionaries.

questions.question: What is the superlative form of 'fat'?
questions.explanation: 'fat' follows the CVC pattern, so we double the 't' and add '-est': 'fattest'.

questions.question: Which is the CORRECT superlative sentence?
options: This is the most interesting book of all.
This is the interestingest book of all.
This is the more interesting book of all.
This is the most interestingest book.
questions.explanation: 'the most interesting' is correct for a multi-syllable adjective in the superlative.

questions.question: Select ALL the correctly formed superlatives.
questions.explanation: 'wisest' (add st), 'biggest' (double + est), and 'most interesting' (use most) are correct. 'beautifullest' is wrong — it should be 'most beautiful'.

questions.question: What is the superlative form of 'fast'?
questions.explanation: The superlative of 'fast' is 'fastest' (add '-est').

questions.topic: Degrees of Comparison: Rules and Usage
questions.question: For a one-syllable adjective ending in consonant-vowel-consonant (like 'big'), what do we do to form the comparative?
options: Double the last consonant and add '-er'
questions.explanation: For CVC adjectives like 'big', we double the last consonant and add '-er': 'bigger'.

questions.topic: Degrees of Comparison: Rules and Usage
questions.question: For an adjective ending in 'e' (like 'wise'), how do we form the comparative?
questions.explanation: For adjectives ending in 'e', we add only 'r': 'wise → wiser'.

questions.topic: Degrees of Comparison: Rules and Usage
questions.question: We never use 'more' or 'most' together with an '-er' or '-est' ending.
questions.explanation: It is incorrect to say 'more taller' or 'most tallest'. We use either the ending OR 'more'/'most', never both.

questions.topic: Degrees of Comparison: Rules and Usage
questions.question: Which sentence has a mistake in the degree of comparison?
options: She is more taller than her sister.
She is taller than her sister.
She is the tallest in her class.
She is as tall as her sister.
questions.explanation: 'more taller' is wrong — we should say just 'taller'. You cannot use 'more' with an '-er' form.

questions.topic: Degrees of Comparison: Rules and Usage
questions.question: When do we use the comparative degree instead of the superlative?
options: When comparing three or more things
questions.explanation: We use the comparative when comparing two things, and the superlative when comparing three or more.

questions.topic: Degrees of Comparison: Rules and Usage
questions.question: Complete the pattern: 'happy → happier → ____'
questions.explanation: The pattern is positive → comparative → superlative: 'happy → happier → happiest'.

questions.topic: Degrees of Comparison: Rules and Usage
questions.question: Complete the pattern: 'interesting → more interesting → ____'
questions.explanation: For long adjectives, the pattern uses 'more' and 'most': 'interesting → more interesting → most interesting'.

questions.topic: Degrees of Comparison: Rules and Usage
questions.question: Adjectives with three or more syllables usually use 'more' and 'most' instead of '-er' and '-est'.
questions.explanation: Longer adjectives (two or more syllables) usually use 'more' for the comparative and 'most' for the superlative.

questions.topic: Degrees of Comparison: Rules and Usage
questions.question: Which degree is used in 'AC was more beneficial than DC in the long run'?
questions.explanation: 'more beneficial than' compares two things (AC and DC), so it is the comparative degree.

questions.topic: Degrees of Comparison: Rules and Usage
questions.question: Which is correct: 'Edison was the ____ inventor of the three'?
questions.explanation: Comparing three inventors needs the superlative 'most successful'.

questions.question: Who was Nikola Tesla?
options: A Serbian-American inventor and electrical engineer
questions.explanation: Nikola Tesla (1856-1943) was a brilliant Serbian-American inventor and electrical engineer.

questions.question: What type of electrical system did Tesla develop?
questions.explanation: Tesla developed alternating current (AC) electrical systems, which won out over Edison's direct current.

questions.question: Whose direct current (DC) system did Tesla's AC win out over?
questions.explanation: Tesla's alternating current (AC) won out over Edison's direct current (DC).

questions.question: Why was AC more beneficial than DC in the long run?
options: It allowed electricity to travel longer distances more cheaply
It used no electricity at all
It only worked over very short distances
questions.explanation: AC allowed electricity to travel longer distances, making it easier and cheaper to power cities and industries, unlike DC which worked only over short distances.

questions.question: Which of these did Tesla create?
options: The Tesla coil and foundations of wireless technology
questions.explanation: Tesla created many inventions, including the Tesla coil, foundations of wireless technology, and early X-ray imaging.

questions.question: About how many patents did Tesla hold?
questions.explanation: Despite his genius, Tesla held over 300 patents but still died in relative poverty.

questions.question: Even though Tesla was a genius with many patents, he died in relative poverty.
questions.explanation: The text says that despite his genius and over 300 patents, Tesla died in relative poverty with many ideas unrealised.

questions.question: What was Tesla's greatest wish, as he told the journalist?
options: To illuminate (light up) the entire Earth
questions.explanation: Tesla said his greatest wish was to illuminate the entire Earth — 'There is enough electricity to create a second sun.'

questions.question: According to Tesla, which came first — energy or matter?
options: Energy came first, and matter was created from it
They appeared at exactly the same time
questions.explanation: Tesla said, 'First was energy, then matter,' explaining that matter is created from original energy we know as light.

questions.question: Whose theory did Tesla strongly oppose in the interview?
questions.explanation: Tesla strongly opposed Einstein's Theory of Relativity, arguing that space is not curved.

questions.question: Tesla compared light and lightning to which art form?
questions.explanation: Tesla said 'light is music' — light particles are like written notes and lightning can be an entire musical piece.

questions.question: The company Tesla, Inc. (founded in 2003) is named after Nikola Tesla.
questions.explanation: Tesla, Inc., a multinational automotive and clean energy company founded in 2003, is named after the inventor Nikola Tesla.

questions.question: What does the interview form of this text mean?
options: It is written as questions from a journalist and answers from Tesla
It is a poem with rhyming lines
It is a list of science facts only
It is a short story with no dialogue
questions.explanation: The text is an interview — a journalist asks Tesla questions and Tesla answers them in a conversation.

questions.question: Tesla said his work laid foundations for which modern fields?
options: Electrical engineering, telecommunications, and renewable energy
questions.explanation: The text says Tesla's work laid crucial foundations for modern electrical engineering, telecommunications, and renewable energy technology.

questions.question: Tesla's visionary concepts were often decades ahead of their time.
questions.explanation: The text states that Tesla's visionary concepts were often decades ahead of their time.

questions.question: In which years did Nikola Tesla live?
questions.explanation: Nikola Tesla lived from 1856 to 1943.

questions.question: Why does the journalist's interview make Tesla's ideas interesting to read?
options: We hear Tesla's own imaginative answers in his own words
It only lists dates and numbers
It hides all of Tesla's opinions
questions.explanation: Through the interview format, we hear Tesla's own imaginative, poetic answers about energy, light, and the universe in his own words.

questions.question: What does 'revolutionised' mean?
options: Completely changed something in a big way
questions.explanation: 'revolutionised' means completely changed something in a big way.

questions.question: What is an 'electrical engineer'?
options: A person who studies and works with electricity and machines
questions.explanation: An 'electrical engineer' is a person who studies and works with electricity and machines.

questions.question: What does 'groundbreaking' mean?
options: Something very new and important that changes how people think or do things
questions.explanation: 'groundbreaking' means something very new and important that changes how people think or do things.

questions.question: What is a 'visionary'?
options: Someone who thinks creatively about the future
questions.explanation: A 'visionary' is someone who thinks creatively about the future.

questions.question: What does 'alternating current (AC)' mean?
options: A type of electricity that changes direction many times every second
A kind of water current in rivers
questions.explanation: 'alternating current (AC)' is a type of electricity that changes direction many times every second.

questions.question: What does 'direct current (DC)' mean?
options: Electricity that flows in one direction
questions.explanation: 'direct current (DC)' is electricity that flows in one direction.

questions.question: What does 'multinational' mean?
options: A company that works in many countries
A company with only one worker
A company that makes only music
A company that has closed down
questions.explanation: 'multinational' describes a company that works in many countries.

questions.question: What does 'illuminate' mean?
options: To light up or make bright
questions.explanation: 'illuminate' means to light up or make bright.

questions.question: What does 'telecommunications' mean?
options: Sending messages or information over long distances (phones, internet)
Talking to someone in the same room
questions.explanation: 'telecommunications' means sending messages or information over long distances, like phones and the internet.

questions.question: What does 'vitality' mean?
options: Energy and strength to live and be active
questions.explanation: 'vitality' means energy and strength to live and be active.

questions.question: What are 'celestial bodies'?
options: Objects in space, like stars, moons, and planets
questions.explanation: 'celestial bodies' are objects in space, like stars, moons, and planets.

questions.question: What is the 'equator'?
options: The line around the middle of the Earth
questions.explanation: The 'equator' is the imaginary line around the middle of the Earth.

questions.question: 'Groundbreaking' work is something new and important that changes how people think.
questions.explanation: 'groundbreaking' describes something very new and important that changes how people think or do things.

questions.question: Which word best replaces 'lit up' in 'The lamp lit up the room'?
questions.explanation: 'illuminated' means lit up or made bright, so it fits best.

questions.question: If an invention 'revolutionised' travel, it ____ travel.
questions.explanation: 'revolutionised' means completely changed in a big way, so the invention completely changed travel.

questions.question: What does the idiom 'put your best foot forward' mean?
options: To try your hardest and make the best impression
questions.explanation: 'put your best foot forward' means to try your hardest and make the best possible impression.

questions.question: What does a 'make-or-break moment' mean?
options: A moment that will decide success or failure
A moment to take a break
A moment to fix a machine
questions.explanation: A 'make-or-break moment' is a crucial moment that will decide whether something succeeds or fails.

questions.question: An idiom is a phrase whose meaning is different from the literal meaning of its words.
questions.explanation: An idiom has a special meaning that is different from the ordinary, literal meaning of its individual words.

questions.question: If you 'give it your all', you ____.
questions.explanation: To 'give it your all' means to put in your full effort and try your very best.

questions.question: In the phrase 'the wings of youth', what idea is being suggested?
options: The energy and freedom of being young
questions.explanation: 'the wings of youth' is a figurative phrase suggesting the energy, freedom, and excitement of being young.

questions.question: The phrase 'like Saturn's rings' is used to describe something that is ____.
options: spread out in a ring shape, like the rings around Saturn
questions.explanation: 'like Saturn's rings' compares something (such as scattered stars) to the beautiful rings spread around the planet Saturn.

questions.question: Figurative phrases like 'the wings of youth' are meant to be understood literally, word for word.
questions.explanation: Figurative phrases are NOT literal — 'the wings of youth' does not mean real wings; it suggests the energy and freedom of youth.

questions.question: In 'Tesla was a brilliant, visionary inventor with over 300 patents', which words are adjectives of quality?
questions.explanation: 'brilliant' and 'visionary' describe the kind of inventor Tesla was, so they are adjectives of quality. '300' is a number adjective.

questions.question: In 'Which brilliant scientist made these three discoveries?', identify the interrogative adjective.
questions.explanation: 'Which' asks a question about the scientist, so it is interrogative. 'brilliant' is quality, 'these' is demonstrative, 'three' is number.

questions.question: What is the comparative form of 'happy'?
questions.explanation: 'happy' ends in 'y', so we change 'y' to 'i' and add 'er': 'happier'.

questions.question: What is the superlative form of 'happy'?
questions.explanation: 'happy' ends in 'y', so we change 'y' to 'i' and add 'est': 'happiest'.

questions.question: Which word describes the kind of energy in 'positive mental energy'?
questions.explanation: 'positive' describes the kind of energy, so it is an adjective of quality. ('mental' also describes the energy.)

questions.topic: Degrees of Comparison: Rules and Usage
questions.question: Complete the pattern: 'good → ____ → best' (an irregular adjective).
questions.explanation: 'good' is irregular: its degrees are 'good → better → best', not 'gooder' or 'goodest'.

questions.topic: Degrees of Comparison: Rules and Usage
questions.question: Complete the pattern: 'bad → worse → ____' (an irregular adjective).
questions.explanation: 'bad' is irregular: its degrees are 'bad → worse → worst'.

questions.question: In 'enough electricity', the word 'enough' is an adjective of quantity used with an uncountable noun.
questions.explanation: 'enough' shows the amount of electricity (quantity), and 'electricity' is uncountable, so this is an adjective of quantity with an uncountable noun.

questions.question: In 'Tesla created numerous inventions', what does 'numerous' show?
questions.explanation: 'numerous' shows a general large quantity (many), acting like an indefinite adjective of number/quantity.

questions.question: In 'That famous inventor held three hundred patents', which word is demonstrative?
questions.explanation: 'That' points out which inventor, so it is a demonstrative adjective. 'famous' is quality, and 'three hundred' shows number.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Tesla's AC was more useful than DC.
Tesla's AC was usefuller than DC.
Tesla's AC was most useful than DC.
Tesla's AC was more usefuller than DC.
questions.explanation: 'useful' has two syllables, so the comparative is 'more useful than'.

questions.question: According to the text, birds came to Tesla's hotel window every ____.
questions.explanation: The journalist notes that birds came to Tesla's hotel window every morning.

questions.question: What does Tesla's answer about light and music suggest about his way of thinking?
options: He saw science and art (like music) as deeply connected
He disliked all forms of music
questions.explanation: By saying 'light is music' and comparing lightning to a musical piece, Tesla shows he saw science and art as deeply connected — a creative, imaginative view.

questions.question: Which word means 'a person who thinks creatively about the future'?
questions.explanation: A 'visionary' is someone who thinks creatively about the future.

questions.question: Which word means 'to light up or make bright'?
questions.explanation: 'illuminate' means to light up or make bright.

questions.question: Which situation best fits the phrase 'put your best foot forward'?
options: Starting a new job and trying to impress your boss
questions.explanation: 'put your best foot forward' fits a situation like starting a new job, where you try your hardest to make a great impression.

questions.question: In 'Which two ancient monuments did those tourists visit?', how many DIFFERENT kinds of adjectives are used?
questions.explanation: 'Which' (interrogative), 'two' (number), 'ancient' (quality), and 'those' (demonstrative) — several different kinds are used.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The cheetah is the fastest predator on land.
The cheetah is the most fastest predator.
The cheetah is the faster predator on land.
The cheetah is fastest than others.
questions.explanation: 'the fastest' is the correct superlative for the one-syllable adjective 'fast'.

questions.question: What does an interview mainly involve?
options: One person asking questions and another answering
questions.explanation: An interview involves one person (the interviewer) asking questions and another person answering them.

questions.question: Tesla believed that matter is an expression of light, and that energy is older than matter.
questions.explanation: Tesla said matter is an expression of infinite forms of light because energy is older than matter.

questions.topic: Degrees of Comparison: Rules and Usage
questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses BOTH a comparative and a superlative?
options: Edison was more successful, but Tesla became the greatest visionary.
Edison was more successfuller than the greatest.
Edison was successful than the most greatest.
Edison was the most success and more great.
questions.explanation: 'more successful' (comparative, two people) and 'the greatest' (superlative, all visionaries) are both used correctly here.

questions.question: Which word means 'a company that works in many countries'?
questions.explanation: 'multinational' describes a company that works in many countries.

questions.question: Tesla's inventions helped power homes worldwide mainly through which system?
questions.explanation: Tesla's alternating current (AC) electrical systems now power homes worldwide.
